title: WALI X
medium: AI Model, Frame, Glass, Computer, Mic
description: WALI X (a conceptual play on the Javanese word walik, meaning reversed) is an interactive artificial intelligence installation that synthesizes the philosophical wisdom of the historical Wali Songo to manifest a digital tenth Wali. Rooted in a typographic ambigram proposing that belief is the essence of technology and technology is the essence of belief, the project draws a profound parallel between the historical use of cultural mediums like wayang and gamelan as transformative communication tools and the contemporary rise of artificial intelligence. Physically, the artwork features framed embroidered textiles that veil an interface displaying real time transcripts and audio waves, effectively creating a digital face for a formless entity. Visitors engage in spoken dialogue by invoking a respectful ancestral greeting to initiate a conversation, prompting the AI to respond with calm and culturally rich Nusantara metaphors that consistently conclude with a reflective inquiry directed back at the user. By functioning as a philosophical mirror rather than an oracle of definitive answers, WALI X challenges participants to deeply consider humanity's position at the complex intersection of technological advancement and spiritual conviction.
exhibition: Surabaya Art Prize - Orasis Art Space — Surabaya

title: Pasax Bumi Sintesis
description: PASAX BUMI SINTESIS is an integrated modular synthesizer developed collaboratively by Awikworks and Bauhouse Consorxium for the performance film The Body Remembers. Designed as an ecological listening instrument rather than a conventional musical device, the system translates real-time environmental conditions—including soil pH, wind, temperature, and bioelectrical signals from living plants—into analog sound. Powered by a self-contained off-grid system, PASAX BUMI SINTESIS establishes a continuous feedback loop between the landscape, the performer, and the instrument, allowing the environment itself to shape the sonic composition. Rejecting fixed scores and predetermined authorship, the work proposes a collaborative relationship in which nature becomes an active agent, transforming the land from a passive backdrop into a living participant whose rhythms, memories, and material conditions continuously compose the performance.

title: AMPRRRONG... (Bytebeat)
medium: Acrylic on Canvas, Bytebeat Album Device
description: AMPRRRONG - 1.618 033 988 749.... (Bytebeat Remix) is an empirical demonstration by Muzeian that synthesizes structural mathematics, generative sound synthesis, and DIY hardware hacking culture. The work explores the transformation of manipulated audio recordings into code-based, deterministic sound synthesis. In this composition, the Fibonacci (Fn) and Lucas (Ln) sequences are mapped directly to drive bitwise logical computations (bytebeat), using the golden ratio ($1.618...$) as the primary parameter to define the sonic architecture, rhythmic structures, and feedback loops across 12 precisely structured audio tracks. Complementing this computational audio dimension, the physical medium consisting of acrylic on canvas serves as a spatial representation of the technical assembly. Featuring a high-contrast duotone (red and blue) visual composition, the canvas projects a low-angle human figure superimposed with interwoven audio cables, effect pedals, and a pack of cigarettes—everyday objects that ground the hardware elements and linear circuits into the reality of daily life, arranged precisely according to the golden ratio.
exhibition: Mukadimah - Artmeru, Malang

title: BLOT
description: BLOT is an interactive zine installation and noise instrument by Muzeian under the experimental sound moniker AMPRRRONG. Rooted in East Java’s underground experimental noise scene, the project explores subgenres like industrial and harsh noise , drawing thematic inspiration from the fluid, ever-flowing nature of the Amprong River in Malang. Printed on transparent vinyl plastic sheets to mirror the accidental ink bleeds and spontaneous, subconscious markings from the artist's notebook , the zine captures the organic inception of the AMPRRRONG logo. In this installation, visitors interact with the zine using a light-sensor-equipped pointer tool (duding) connected to a synthesizer.
exhibition: The Right to Slow Down - Artchemist — Tujujati - Surabaya

title: Sukatani 1312 Matches
description: Sukatani 1312 Matches was created for Habis Gelap Terbitlah Gelap, a collective exhibition responding to the silencing of Sukatani's song Bayar, Bayar, Bayar. Transforming an ordinary matchbox into a piece of visual propaganda, the work proposes that even the smallest spark can ignite collective resistance. Like a single match capable of starting a larger fire, it reflects how images, symbols, and acts of solidarity can spread beyond institutional control, turning everyday objects into catalysts for dissent.
exhibition: Habis Gelap Terbitlah Gelap - LIB — Yogyakarta

title: Cethik Geni
description: Cethik Geni is an interactive installation inspired by cethik geni, a traditional Javanese practice of igniting a wood-fired stove by blowing air through a small bamboo tube. This humble daily ritual serves as a point of departure for reflecting on the paradoxical relationship between wind and fire, elements that can either sustain or extinguish one another depending on circumstance. Expanding this metaphor, the work draws from the Obor Suroan ritual in Pasuruan, East Java, where villagers carry torches while guiding trance dancers toward a sacred tree believed to be inhabited by a guardian spirit. Within this ritual, fire symbolizes both illumination and destruction, while wind becomes an unseen force capable of nurturing or erasing the flame, echoing the ways human judgment often shifts according to desire and consequence. The installation invites visitors to blow through a bamboo pipe to activate a hidden light within the artwork, reenacting the gesture of *cethik geni* and transforming breath into a performative act of participation. By intertwining Javanese ritual, ecological knowledge, and interactive technology, Cethik Geni explores the fragile balance between humans, nature, and spirituality, revealing how cultural traditions continue to embody reciprocal relationships between the visible and the invisible, the material and the immaterial.
exhibition: Media X Space: Beyond Illumination - Binus University × Arcolabs × CG Artspace — Jakarta

title: MTN LAB: Bootleg
description: MTN Lab: Bootleg Merchandise Residency is a self-critical artistic project that examines how contemporary art residencies are often reduced to formal documentation and institutional outcomes. Developed during a residency in Gresik, Indonesia, the project involved collecting everyday objects from streets, markets, industrial sites, and coastal areas, treating them as material evidence of lived experience. Half of these findings were transformed into handmade paper used for branding and documentation, while the remaining objects were packaged as the contents of fictional merchandise. Presented as a commercial retail booth complete with product displays, collaborator certificates, branded packaging, and an administrative desk, the installation blurs the boundaries between artwork, documentation, and commodity. By mimicking the language and aesthetics of commercial merchandising, MTN Lab: Bootleg Merchandise Residency questions how artistic experiences are archived, authenticated, and ultimately commodified within contemporary art systems.
exhibition: MTN Lab - Kemenbud, Gresik

title: Bocil Kematian
description: Bocil Kematian is a sculptural figure that emerged unexpectedly during a studio cleanup. Formed from leftover materials and found objects, the work was recognized rather than intentionally constructed. Its childlike yet eerie presence transforms discarded remnants into a character that feels both familiar and unsettling. By preserving this accidental formation, the sculpture reflects on the role of chance, intuition, and observation in the creative process, revealing how meaning can emerge from the most ordinary materials and moments.

title: Awikworks Tarsah Sintesis
description: Awikworks Tarsah/hasraT is an ongoing modular synthesizer project that functions as both a sonic instrument and a personal archive of desire, obsession, and continuous exploration. The title combines tarsah (read backwards: hasrat) which mean desire, reflecting an impulse that never fully settles and constantly seeks new forms of expression. Conceived as an ever-expanding system, the project resists completion, growing organically through the addition of self-built modules, experiments, and evolving ideas. Many of its visual and conceptual elements draw inspiration from figures and narratives that have shaped my imagination, including Motoko Kusanagi from Ghost in the Shell, Shotaro Kaneda and Tetsuo Shima from Akira, Miyamoto Musashi from Vagabond, as well as cultural references such as Hausu (1977), The Holy Mountain (1973), Perfect Blue (1997), They Live (1988), and the legendary East Javanese comedian Cak Kartolo. These influences are translated into circuits, interfaces, and sound processes, forming a constellation of personal references that continuously mutate over time. Rather than a finished object, Awikworks Tarsah/hasraT exists as a living framework for experimentation, embodying a relentless creative drive that persists without a final destination.

title: POV JATIM
description: POV JAWA TIMUR is an audiovisual installation that presents a miniature portrait of contemporary popular culture in East Java through the phenomenon of *Sound Horeg*, a grassroots sound system culture that has recently gained widespread attention on social media. The work originates from observations of community-built sound systems commonly found at local celebrations, street parades, and public entertainment events throughout the Malang region and its surrounding areas. Derived from the words *sound* and *horeg*, a local term meaning “to vibrate,” Sound Horeg refers to powerful custom-built speaker systems capable of producing bass frequencies intense enough to shake windows, rooftops, and entire neighborhoods. Typically assembled through collective effort and mounted on trucks, these mobile sound systems have become a distinctive cultural attraction, reflecting local creativity, technical ingenuity, and communal identity. Through an immersive combination of sound, moving images, and spatial experience, POV JAWA TIMUR explores how technology, spectacle, and participation shape emerging cultural practices in contemporary society. The installation serves both as a documentation of a uniquely East Javanese phenomenon and as a reflection on the social dynamics, aspirations, and collective expressions that continue to define the region’s cultural landscape today.
exhibition: Finna Art of The Year 2025 - Orasis Art Space — Surabaya
pdf: pdf/KATALOG FINNA ART OF THE YEAR 2025.pdf

title: PKL
description: Awikworks PKL (Penyintesis Kaki Lima) is a handcrafted synthesizer that embodies the idea of synthesis, bringing together disparate materials, ideas, and experiences to create something entirely new. Inspired by my fascination with electronic sound synthesis and shaped by the limitations of accessing commercial synthesizers, this project emerged from a self-driven process of building and modifying electronic modules from scratch. Many of the components, materials, and inspirations were discovered in the everyday environment of Indonesia’s kaki lima (sidewalks and informal street spaces), where discarded objects and overlooked resources become catalysts for experimentation. By assembling these findings into a functional sound instrument, Awikworks PKL transforms the spirit of the street into an electronic system of creative possibilities. The work reflects a personal journey of resourcefulness, adaptation, and continuous experimentation, demonstrating how technology, local culture, and imagination can be synthesized into a singular artistic and sonic experience.
exhibition: Bebunyian Sound Art Festival - Korean Cultural Center × Baseline Studio — Surabaya

title: ANTI-IDOL
description: Amprrrong: Anti-Idol is a multimedia installation and experimental music project that emerged from Muhammad Zeian’s long-standing engagement with idol culture since 2011. Consisting of a nine-track album, listening station and painting by Urubingwaru, the work introduces Anti-Idol as both a fictional persona and a critical framework for rethinking the conventions of idol music and fandom. Through a composition of noise, irregular scales, fragmented conversations, and abrasive sonic textures, the project deliberately departs from the polished aesthetics commonly associated with idol performances. Presented alongside visual elements inspired by underground music culture, Anti-Idol draws attention to the tensions between admiration and exploitation, spectacle and labor, fantasy and reality. While inspired by the artist’s experience as a wota, the work also examines the industrial mechanisms that sustain idol culture, where youth, intimacy, and constant visibility become commodities. By embracing noise as a form of resistance and experimentation, Amprrrong: Anti-Idol challenges audiences to look beyond the cheerful surface of entertainment culture and confront the social, economic, and emotional structures that exist beneath it.
exhibition: Anti Idol — Amprrrong Showcase - Korean Cultural Center × Baseline Studio — Surabaya

title: Adblock
description: Adblock Enabled is a digitally manipulated photographic series that offers a critical commentary on the escalating issue of visual pollution in urban environments. Conceived as a direct response to the overwhelming proliferation of illegal political banners that relentlessly clutter public spaces, the project uses digital intervention to visually reclaim these shared areas. By conceptually blocking these intrusive and unauthorized advertisements, the series highlights the aggressive nature of modern political campaigning while inviting viewers to reflect on the profound aesthetic and psychological impacts of visual noise in our daily surroundings.

title: Oprex Budoyo
description: Awikworks Oprex Budoyo is a dynamic workshop and multimedia installation that channels the vibrant energy of East Javanese subculture to foster an open, collaborative artistic community. Rooted deeply in the traditional art of Bantengan, the project translates this rich cultural heritage into a contemporary context by adopting a self-sufficient electronic approach built entirely from PCBs and customized electrical components. This synthesis of past and present highlights how traditional artistic objects can organically evolve beyond conventional boundaries when fueled by a shared do-it-yourself spirit. By combining various communal activities and integrating an immersive, Bantengan-inspired soundscape composed by TamaT, the installation transforms into a joyful cultural event that not only sustains the historical creative energy of the region but also resonates profoundly with the modern zeitgeist.
exhibition: Jogja Biennale — Asana Bina Seni (Se)tempat - Yogyakarta

title: Kabesha
description: Inspired by the lyrics of Shonichi—“Through rigorous practice, I surpass my own limits” and “Like a flower slowly blooming, hard work will never betray you”—this etched PCB artwork reflects the journey of an idol whose growth is shaped by persistence, discipline, and continuous self-improvement. The intricate circuit pathways symbolize the countless hours of training, challenges, and aspirations that gradually form an individual's path toward their dreams. Just as electronic circuits rely on connections to function, an idol’s career is built through dedication, support, and repeated effort over time. By translating these ideas into the language of electronic fabrication, Blooming Circuit celebrates perseverance as an invisible yet essential force behind personal transformation, reminding us that meaningful growth often occurs slowly, one step at a time, until it finally blossoms into achievement.
exhibition: 7an - n0lkecil, Surabaya

title: Bengox
description: Bengox is a collaborative project between Awikworks and Dongker, a punk band from Bandung, West Java, that explores the intersection of DIY technology, performance, and music culture. Conceived as a wearable electronic instrument, the work integrates custom-built sound-reactive circuits and LED lights into a balaclava mask, transforming the performer’s voice into a dynamic visual experience. The system responds in real time to speaking, shouting, and singing, creating an immediate connection between sound, movement, and light. Rooted in the DIY ethos shared by both punk culture and open-source electronics, Bengox celebrates experimentation, self-production, and collective creativity while reimagining the body as a site where technology, identity, and performance converge.
exhibition: Pestapora 2023 - Jakarta

title: Penduso Table Game
description: Penduso Table Game (Coffin Table Game) was created in response to the Kanjuruhan Stadium tragedy in Malang, East Java, one of the deadliest disasters in football history. The work serves as both a memorial and a critical reflection on the chain of decisions, systems, and authorities that contributed to the loss of more than a hundred lives. By transforming the logic of a table game into a symbolic space of inquiry, the installation invites viewers to consider how responsibility is distributed and obscured within complex social and institutional structures. Rather than focusing solely on the event itself, the work questions who the real “players” are behind such a humanitarian catastrophe, highlighting the tension between accountability, power, and the value of human life.
exhibition: Lidos Toys Fest - Malng Creative  Center

title: Borongan
description: Kuproy Series explores the figure of the kuli proyek (construction laborer) as a reflection of contemporary social realities in Indonesia. Inspired by the visual language of Soviet socialist realism, the work reinterprets labor imagery through relief sculptures, internet memes, and immersive media. The project emerged from observations of how construction workers frequently appear in social media culture, where they are often reduced to humorous stereotypes and viral content, despite the essential role they play in shaping the built environment. By combining reliefs cast in cement with memes and 360-degree video, the series creates a dialogue between historical representations of labor and contemporary digital culture. Rather than treating workers as objects of entertainment, Kuproy Series seeks to foreground their dignity, resilience, and everyday experiences, highlighting the often-overlooked individuals whose labor underpins the construction of cities, infrastructures, and modern society itself.

title: Singup
description: There is no exact equivalent for singup in Indonesian or English. Singup is an interactive installation inspired by the Javanese word singup, a term that describes an unsettling atmosphere created by silence, darkness, and a sense of uncertainty. Presented in a traditional market in Malang, the work responds to the market’s deteriorating condition and lack of public facilities. Through sensors, sound, and light, the installation evokes a feeling of unease while drawing a parallel between physical space and personal experience. The phrase “This market is singup like my unknown future” reflects the artist’s contemplation of uncertainty, positioning the neglected market as a metaphor for an unpredictable future and the anxieties that accompany it.
exhibition: Nendes Kombet - Pasar Bareng, Malang

title: Modular Miskin
description: Began as a personal exploration into building a modular synthesizer independently. Originally named Modular Miskin, the project was later renamed Awikworks, adopting the motto “low tech-high five” as a reflection of its playful and resourceful approach to technology. Built around open-source principles, the project combines self-assembled electronic modules with repurposed components salvaged from discarded devices. Through experimentation, modification, and reuse, Awikworks transforms everyday electronic waste into functional sound instruments, celebrating DIY culture, accessibility, and creative technological practice.

title: Kydunk Cyberpunk
description: Created during the COVID-19 pandemic, Kydunk Cyberpunk responds to the widespread atmosphere of fear and uncertainty that extended from urban centers to rural communities. In an era of rapid information exchange, anxiety and panic spread as quickly as the virus itself, gradually eroding collective resilience. Drawing inspiration from traditional Javanese practices of tolak bala (rituals for warding off misfortune), the work revisits cultural knowledge that has become increasingly marginalized in contemporary life. Motivated by concerns over the social and psychological impacts of the pandemic, Muzeian reinterprets Rumekso Ing Wengi, a protective kidung (traditional Javanese sung poetry) attributed to Sunan Kalijaga, as a contemporary artistic medium. In Kydunk Cyberpunk, the sound waves of the Rumekso Ing Wengi kidung are transformed into a dynamic field of light, creating a symbolic “light fence” that references the protective function of the original chant. Traditionally believed to safeguard individuals from visible and invisible disturbances, the kidung is reimagined here not as a magical instrument, but as a source of reflection, hope, and psychological resilience. By combining traditional spiritual practices with contemporary media technology, Kydunk Cyberpunk explores how cultural heritage can be reinterpreted to address present-day anxieties. The work ultimately suggests that tradition is not merely a relic of the past, but a living form of wisdom that offers guidance in navigating uncertainty and change.
exhibition: SUMONAR Festival 2020 — Mantra Lumina - sumonarfest.com

title: DJ MI$$$KIN
description: DJ MI$$$KIN is a collaborative audiovisual collage project centered on the vibrant grassroots culture of East Java. By deliberately utilizing a simple medium and relying entirely on a smartphone, the project maximizes the raw creative potential of everyday, accessible tools. Driven by the core philosophy 'miskin benda bukan hatinya' (poor in possessions, but rich in heart), DJ MI$$$KIN serves as an authentic expression of the human spirit and the resilience of a Third World lifestyle.

title: River View Simulation
description: River Viewer Simulator (RVS) is an interactive installation designed to simulate the experience of observing and engaging with a river environment. Through a custom-built sensor controller and digital interface, visitors are invited to interact with a mediated representation of a river rather than the river itself. Although the system provides a control unit, participants never possess complete control over the experience. Every interaction triggers a chain of programmed responses that imitate the cause-and-effect relationships found in natural environments. The work questions the extent to which technological simulations can reproduce ecological experiences and explores the gap between direct observation and mediated perception. By reconstructing a river through digital processes, River Viewer Simulator reflects on how contemporary technologies shape our understanding of nature, transforming lived experiences into controlled, interpretable, and often incomplete representations.
exhibition: Brantastude: Research - Kolekjos, Malang

title: Private (Public) Data
description: Social media has become one of the most dominant forms of communication in contemporary society. Through these platforms, users actively participate, share information, and build networks. In doing so, they continuously generate and contribute personal data, ranging from identity information submitted during registration to behavioral data produced through everyday online activities. While this accumulation of data often remains invisible to the public, it forms extensive databases that can be analyzed, categorized, and utilized with increasing precision. As personal information becomes more accessible and valuable, concerns regarding privacy, surveillance, and data exploitation continue to grow. Private (Public) Data reflects on this condition through a visual exploration of the blurred boundary between private and public identity in the digital age. The work emerges from a sense of anxiety toward increasingly systematic forms of data collection and processing. It questions how willingly we surrender personal information to digital platforms, often without fully understanding how it is stored, interpreted, or used. The body imagery presented in this work symbolizes personal identities that have become transparent, exposed, and publicly accessible through social media networks, revealing the fragile nature of privacy in contemporary digital culture.
exhibition: Five Passages to The Future - Arcolabs, Galeri Nasional Indonesia

title: Oxymeter Fog
medium: Oxygen Saturation Data, Arduino Oxymeter Sensor, PC, Projection, Photo.
description: Born into an era where technology is widely accessible, I often assume that millions of people share equal opportunities to access information and technological advancement. This assumption led me to an interest in new media art as a medium for questioning and reflecting on contemporary realities.Created during the XPLORE: New Media Art Incubation program under the theme “Eco-Data,” Oxymeter Fog explores environmental conditions in Yogyakarta through data-driven artistic practice. The work utilizes a custom-built device developed using Arduino components and computer coding to collect and process environmental data, particularly related to air quality. The collected data is translated into an aesthetic experience, allowing visitors to encounter environmental conditions through sensory interpretation rather than scientific visualization alone. Oxymeter Fog functions as a brief discourse on the discrepancy between appearance and reality, suggesting that the environment around us may not be as pristine as it seems.
exhibition: XPLORE: New Media Art Incubation — Unearthing The Unknown - Arcolabs  × HONF, Yogyakarta

title: Klinik Alternatip "Pixel Scan"
description: In collaboration with Zuhkhriyan Zakaria, M. Azhar Hammadi and Arif Prasetyo, Klinik Alternatip - Pixel Scan is an interactive visual installation that utilizes a custom sensor to project an individual's conceptual aura color through a simplified LED matrix display. By presenting the audience with these chromatic suggestions regarding their own physical and energetic states, the artwork serves as an engaging psychological prompt designed to gauge public attitudes toward rapid contemporary technological advancements. The project is deeply rooted in a critical exploration of digital literacy and technological disparity, emphasizing the stark reality that society does not share equal access or experience with modern innovations. Ultimately, the piece functions as a provocative commentary on how this unequal distribution of technological understanding is frequently exploited by certain entities for manipulative purposes, inviting viewers to critically reassess their own vulnerabilities and relationships with the pervasive digital systems of the modern era.
exhibition: Pekan Seni Media 2019 — Sinkronik, Kemdikbud — Samarinda

title: Sarung
description: Sarung is a conceptual artwork that explores the resilient and enduring sartorial culture of the Tenggerese people through their most ubiquitous traditional garment. Fundamentally defined as a wide tubular cloth sewn at both ends, the sarong boasts a minimalist design that provides a multitude of practical functions for the Tengger tribe, effortlessly transforming into a makeshift jacket, bag, head covering, or prayer attire. Beyond its utilitarian value, the garment carries profound and often contrasting symbolic weight, being historically associated with both sacred religious rituals and clandestine activities. Visually, the piece utilizes a series of printed antonyms to signify its universal nature, illustrating that the sarong transcends social divides and is worn by individuals from all walks of life regardless of their differences. By integrating modern corporate outdoor brand logos and contemporary design elements into this traditional canvas, the artwork serves as a compelling reflection of the current era, highlighting how a deeply rooted cultural artifact continuously adapts to modern consumerism while maintaining its essential identity and function.
exhibition: Dendang Calon Guru, 8 Kota - Universitas Negeri Yogyakarta

title: Komposisi Hewani
medium: Single Track, Photo, Vynil, CD, Cassete
description: Komposisi Hewani is a cross-species and cross-disciplinary collaborative project that culminates in a unique musical single exploring the speculative premise of animal sentience and vocalization. Imagining a reality where animals possess high intelligence and the ability to speak, the work gives voice to their hypothetical protests against the profound inequality existing between their kind and humanity. Driven by a poignant critique of escalating human selfishness and the severe, ongoing degradation of our ecosystems, the project channels these non-human grievances into a compelling auditory narrative. Developed in collaboration with Muzeian and Misbo for the Art Edu Care: Everyday Art exhibition, this thought-provoking piece challenges audiences to confront the destructive consequences of anthropocentrism through an imaginative and deeply reflective auditory experience.
exhibition: Art Edu Care, Universitas Sebelas Maret — Solo

title: Proyek Rekapitulasi Senyum
description: Proyek Rekapitulasi Senyum (Smile Recapitulation Project) is a participatory art project presented as a small village office, inviting exhibition visitors to contribute their smiles through photographic portraits. Grounded in the idea that artistic meaning can be produced collectively between artist and participant, the work accumulates smiling faces from diverse individuals and backgrounds to reveal a simple yet universal truth: we smile in the same language. By gathering and displaying these expressions, the project highlights the smile as a shared human gesture that transcends cultural, social, and personal differences, reminding us of our common humanity and our capacity for connection.
exhibition: Abnormal Project Annual #2 — Universitas Negeri Malang

title: Communication Breakdown
medium: Wheatpaste on Wood Board, Microphone Apps
description: Inspired by Stephen R. Covey, “The biggest communication problem is we do not listen to understand. We listen to reply,” This interactive installation invites visitors to speak into the system. After a brief delay, their words are repeated back to them, creating a simple feedback loop. The work serves as a metaphor for communication that prioritizes reaction over understanding, highlighting how messages can be echoed without being truly heard. Through this interaction, Communication Breakdown encourages reflection on the importance of listening as the foundation of meaningful dialogue and human connection.
exhibition: NOV ART, Art Techno — Universitas Negeri Malang
